mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with declining FEDFUNDS, or rank correlation between FEDFUNDS trend and SPX returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it triggers aggressive monetary tightening that increases real borrowing costs and depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for 2 consecutive months, or rank correlation between FEDFUNDS threshold and SPX returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in nonfarm payrolls indicates accelerating labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of UNRATE decline and PAYEMS increase fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or interaction term in SPX return regression is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes with high housing starts and robust retail sales, the S&P 500 underperforms as recession risks rise and monetary policy tightens, generating negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods, or rank correlation between demand regime and SPX returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with rising UNRATE, or rank correlation between UNRATE trend and SPX returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 110.0 for two consecutive months, it indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with INDPRO < 110.0 for 2 consecutive months, or rank correlation between INDPRO threshold and SPX returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and GDP growth signals broad economic contraction that increases recession probability and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of INDPRO decline and GDPC1 slowdown fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or interaction term in SPX return regression is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve implements aggressive tightening that raises real interest rates and reduces equity multiples, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with CPIAUCSL > 3.0% yoy, or rank correlation between CPIAUCSL threshold and SPX returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
